Method

Definitions and caveats

Income
Total income from HESA Table 1: tuition fees, funding body grants, research grants, other income, investment income, donations and endowments.
Academic delivery
Academic departments (teaching and departmental research, HESA cost centres 101–145) plus research grants and contracts (207).
Support services
Academic services (201: library, central IT and computing, learning resources) plus general education expenditure (203: bursaries, scholarships, examinations) and staff and student facilities (204).
Management and administration
Central administration and services (202).
Estates
Premises (205): running costs, repairs and maintenance, depreciation and finance costs on the estate.
Residences and other
Residences and catering operations (206) and other expenditure (208, excluding the pension cost adjustment).
Pension adjustments
The non-cash pension cost adjustment reported in Table 8 (USS, LGPS and similar provision movements). These swing year to year: Reading's was +£72.6m in 2021/22 and −£102.7m in 2023/24. They are excluded by default; switch to Included to match the audited accounts.
Surplus or deficit
Income minus expenditure (operating result before gains, losses, tax and joint ventures). The surplus and deficit filter uses this figure, so it follows the pension setting.
Capital investment
HESA Table 9 total actual capital spend, split into buildings and equipment plus intangible assets. Capital spend is lumpy, so the 3-year average divides three years of spend by three years of income.
Averages
Provider average gives each provider equal weight. Pooled £ adds up money across the group, so large providers dominate. The benchmark is always excluded from group and sector averages; medians appear on the distribution chart.
Mission groups
Memberships as at 2026, applied to every year. "Reading comparators" is a starting peer set of research-intensive universities outside the Russell Group; edit data/mission_groups.csv to change it.
Coverage
From 2018/19 some English providers didn't have to report the subject (cost centre) breakdown, and providers that joined later or haven't yet reported a year are missing from it. Small and specialist providers are excluded by default through the minimum income filter.
Institution detail tab
Breaks each Overview heading into HESA Table 8 activity lines and types of cost (staff, operating, depreciation, interest). Research cost recovery compares research grant income (Table 1) with research grant spend. Residences and catering are shown net of their income (Table 7). Gaps are differences in pence per £1 of income, so providers of different sizes compare fairly. Providers that don't report a breakdown are left out of that line's average.
Subjects tab
Academic department spend and research income by HESA cost centre (Tables 8 and 5), set against student enrolments by subject (Student Table 49, full-time plus half of part-time, all levels). Cost centres and CAH subjects are matched into nine broad areas: medicine, health and psychology (101–107 / CAH 01, 02, 04); biosciences, agriculture, vet and sport (108–110, 112 / 03, 05, 06); physical and environmental sciences and maths (111, 113, 114, 122, 124 / 07, 09, 26); engineering and computing (115–121 / 10, 11); architecture and built environment (123 / 13); social sciences and law (127–132 / 15, 16); business and management (133–134 / 17); education (135–136 / 22, 23); arts, humanities and languages (125–126, 137–145 / 19, 20, 24, 25). Providers code staff and spend to cost centres in different ways, so treat single-subject outliers with care. Subject comparisons use medians.
Source
HESA Higher Education Provider Data: Finance, Tables 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 14 (2015/16 to 2024/25, last updated May 2026), and HESA Student Table 49 (January 2026). Licensed under CC BY 4.0. All money is in £ thousands at source.
